<ExternalIntegrationHeader slug="dyson" />

This integration connects Gladys to your connected **Dyson purifiers, fans and
heaters** (Pure Cool, Purifier Cool, Hot+Cool, Humidify+Cool, Big+Quiet and
the older "Link" models). Turn them on and off, set the speed, oscillation,
night mode and heating, and follow the air quality they measure.

## What you need

- A **MyDyson** account (the Dyson mobile app), with your devices already
  added and connected to Wi-Fi.
- The e-mail address and password of that account.
- Access to the account's mailbox: Dyson e-mails a **one-time code** at every
  sign-in.

## Local and cloud

The integration can reach a device in two ways:

- **Local**: straight over your network (MQTT, port 1883). Fast, and it works
  without Internet. Give the device address in the configuration (see
  **Settings** below).
- **Dyson cloud**: through Dyson's servers, from anywhere. Needs Internet and
  a signed-in account.

The Dyson account is always needed once: it gives the list of devices and the
local password of each one.

On the Configuration screen, the **Prefer the local connection** toggle (on by
default) picks the path tried first. The other one is the fallback. Each
device shows a **badge** with the path in use: local, cloud or unreachable. An
**orange dot** on the badge means "it works, but through the fallback": hover
it to see why.

## Getting started

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations → Dyson → Configuration**.
2. Fill in:
   - **MyDyson e-mail**: the e-mail of your account;
   - **MyDyson password**;
   - **Account country**: the two-letter code of the country chosen when the
     account was created (`FR`, `BE`, `CH`, `GB`, `US`...).
3. Click **Save**.
4. Click **Receive a code**. Dyson e-mails you a 6-digit code.
5. In **Validate the code**, type that code and confirm. The message says how
   many devices were found.
6. Open the **Discover** tab and add your devices.
7. For the local connection, type the address of each device in **Device
   addresses** (see **Settings**), then save.

The session is kept: no new code is needed after a restart. If Dyson ends the
session (a password change, for instance), the connection status asks for a
new code.

## What you get

Depending on the model:

| Feature                               | Models                                    |
| ------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| On / off                              | all                                       |
| Mode list (off, low, medium, high...) | all                                       |
| Speed (1 to 10)                       | all                                       |
| Auto mode                             | all                                       |
| Oscillation                           | all                                       |
| Oscillation angle (45°, 90°, 180°...) | Pure Cool, Purifier Cool, Hot+Cool towers |
| Night mode                            | all                                       |
| Airflow direction (front / back)      | Pure Cool, Purifier Cool, Hot+Cool        |
| Heating + target (°C)                 | Hot+Cool                                  |
| Humidification                        | Humidify+Cool                             |
| Temperature, humidity                 | all                                       |
| PM2.5, PM10 (µg/m³)                   | 2018 and later models                     |
| VOC index, NO2 index                  | 2018 and later models (VOC only on Link)  |
| Formaldehyde (mg/m³)                  | "Formaldehyde" models (K suffix)          |
| Filter life                           | % (HEPA, carbon), hours on Link models    |

The feature names are in French when the account country is French-speaking
(France, Belgium, Switzerland, Luxembourg, Monaco), in English otherwise. A
device already added keeps its names: rename a feature in the device page
(Integrations → Dyson → Devices). In a "Devices" box, Gladys names a feature
that is the only one of its kind after its type ("Selection" for the
oscillation angle): give the row a name of your own in the box settings.

The values are the ones the MyDyson app shows. The VOC and NO2 indexes are
Dyson's: from 0 (clean air) to 10, as whole numbers like in the app.

Choosing a speed turns the device on and the auto mode off, like the remote
does. In auto mode, no speed is shown.

The **mode list** works like the Matter fans: Off, Low (speed 1), Medium
(speed 5), High (speed 10) and Auto. It follows the speed, so the list and the
slider always agree: speeds 1 to 3 show Low, 4 to 6 Medium, 7 to 10 High.
The airflow direction is a list too. Oscillation and night mode are on / off
switches.

The **oscillation angle** list offers the widths of the Dyson app: 45°, 90°,
180° and 350°. Choosing one starts the oscillation, around the direction the
device points to. To stop it, use the Oscillation switch. A width set
otherwise (another app) shows no entry in the list.

**Device added before this version?** Open the **Discover** tab and click
**Update** on the device to get the latest features (oscillation angle,
switches, PM and humidity icons). Its history and scenes are kept. The button shows up as soon as the integration
has restarted in its new version.

Gladys shows the state the device **confirms**: an order the device refused
never shows as done. A change made with the remote or the Dyson app shows up
in Gladys too.

## Scenes

### Triggers

In the scene editor, **Integrations** category:

- **Air quality changed**: the level measured by a device changes. Levels:
  good, fair, poor, very poor. The worst of PM2.5, PM10, VOC and NO2 decides,
  with the bands of the Dyson app (PM2.5: 35 / 53 / 70 µg/m³; PM10: 50 / 75 /
  100 µg/m³; VOC and NO2: 3 / 6 / 8). Variables: `level`, `previous_level`,
  `pm25`, `pm10`, `voc`, `no2`.
- **Filter to replace soon**: a filter goes under 10 % (400 hours on the Link
  models). Variables: `filter` (`hepa`, `carbon`, `combined`), `remaining`.
- **Connection changed**: a device switches to local, to the cloud, or
  becomes unreachable. Variables: `transport`, `previous_transport`,
  `degraded`.

Each trigger can be limited to one device. One event per change. At startup,
the first value is the reference: a restart does not run your scenes again.

### Actions

- **Apply Dyson settings**: power, mode (auto / manual), speed, oscillation
  and night mode, in one order. An empty field changes nothing. "Off" ignores
  the other settings.
- **Set the sleep timer**: the device turns itself off after N minutes (1 to
  540); 0 cancels the timer.

Both return `sent` (order sent or not) and `transport` (connection used). An
unreachable device does not fail the scene: `sent` is then `false`.

## Dashboard widgets

Each widget shows one device, chosen in its settings.

**Dyson air quality**:

- up to 6 live tiles: PM2.5, PM10, VOC, NO2, temperature, humidity (depending
  on the model). Each pollutant tile takes the colour of its level: green
  (good), blue (fair), orange (poor), red (very poor), with the thresholds of
  the scenes below;
- the status: overall air quality (the worst pollutant), formaldehyde on the K
  models, connection, filter life (the filters are what cleans the air);
- a button to refresh the readings.

Dyson gives no single AQI number: the overall level is computed from the four
pollutants.

**Dyson controls**:

- one tile: the fan (off, auto, or a live speed gauge). The air readings are
  in the air quality widget;
- the status: oscillation (with its angle), night mode, airflow, heating,
  connection, sleep timer. With the oscillation buttons, the
  oscillation and night mode rows are left out: the buttons show them;
- four buttons, chosen in the widget's **Buttons** setting:
  - **On/off, auto, speed - and +** (default): turn on / off, auto mode (or
    back to manual), speed - and speed +;
  - **On/off, oscillation, night mode, airflow**: a setting that is on is a
    filled button, a click switches it. On the models that blow one way, the
    auto mode takes the place of the airflow.

After a click, the widget updates as soon as the device answered. To get both
button sets, add the widget twice.

Gladys allows four buttons per widget. To control everything in one place
(mode list, speed slider, oscillation, night mode, airflow), also add the
device to a "Devices" box of your dashboard.

## Settings

- **Device addresses (local)**: the address of each device on your network,
  as `serial=IP`, separated by commas. Example:
  `NK6-EU-MHA0000A=192.168.1.20`. With a single Dyson device in the account,
  the address alone is enough: `192.168.1.20`. A device without an address
  here goes through the Dyson cloud (badge with an orange dot); the badge
  message and **Test the connection** give the serial to type. The serial number is on
  the device label and in the MyDyson app. Give the device a fixed address in
  your router so it does not change.

  To find the address, look at the list of connected devices of your router:
  the device usually shows up under its serial number. The integration
  cannot find it on its own yet: Gladys does not allow it to listen to the
  `_dyson_mqtt._tcp` announcements the devices send.

- **Sensor refresh (s)**: how often the air quality sensors are read, from 15
  to 3600 seconds (60 by default). Power, speed and other changes arrive at
  once, without waiting.

## Buttons

- **Receive a code** / **Validate the code**: sign in to the Dyson account.
- **Test the connection**: reads the account's device list again and shows,
  for each device, the path in use (local, Dyson cloud, unreachable) and,
  on a fallback, why.
- **Sign out**: deletes the token and the device list kept by the
  integration. The devices stay in Gladys.

## Troubleshooting

- **"Dyson refused the code or the password"**: check the saved password,
  then ask for a new code. A code is only valid for a few minutes.
- **No code received**: look in the spam folder, and check the e-mail and the
  country of the account.
- **"cloud" badge with an orange dot**: the device address is missing from
  **Device addresses**, or the local connection was refused (wrong address,
  device on another network Gladys cannot reach). A factory reset changes the device's local password: click
  **Test the connection** to read it again. When the local connection failed
  (device restarting, Wi-Fi down), the integration tries it again every 4
  minutes and goes back to it on its own.
- **"unreachable" badge**: the device is unplugged, off Wi-Fi, or neither the
  local network nor the cloud answers. The integration keeps retrying.
- **The "Air quality" widget tiles stay blue**: with the Gladys "glass" theme,
  the colour of the tile icons is not applied (to be fixed in Gladys). The
  overall level keeps its colour in the status.
- **A sensor stays empty**: some sensors need a few minutes after power-up. A
  model without that sensor never sends a value.

The integration logs (**Supervision** tab) give the details. They never
contain your password or your token.

## Privacy

Your e-mail and password are only sent to Dyson (`appapi.cp.dyson.com`). The
session token and the device list are kept in the integration's data volume,
readable by the integration only.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Dyson asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Getting started | `section` | No | 1. Enter the e-mail, password and country of your MyDyson account, then save. 2. Click "Receive a code": Dyson e-mails you a code. 3. Type it in "Validate the code". 4. Add your devices from the Discover tab. To drive a device on your local network, give its address below; otherwise it goes through the Dyson cloud. |
| MyDyson e-mail | `string` | Yes |  |
| MyDyson password | `secret` | Yes | Only sent to Dyson, with the e-mailed code, to sign in. |
| Account country | `string` | Yes | Two-letter code of the country of the MyDyson account (FR, BE, CH, GB, US...). |
| Device addresses (local) | `string` | No | For the local connection: serial=IP of each device, separated by commas (the IP alone with a single device). Without it: Dyson cloud. |
| Sensor refresh (s) | `number` | No | How often the air quality sensors are read, in seconds. |

## How to install Dyson in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Dyson appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/prohand/gladys-dyson:1.4.0`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/prohand/gladys-dyson](https://github.com/prohand/gladys-dyson).

Dyson requires Gladys `>=5.1.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Dyson is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [prohand](https://github.com/prohand), not by the Gladys core team.
